title: Cokret Event Envelope
description:
Single canonical wire object for **durable Event Envelope** — i.e. events with wire_scope=durable_event OR wire_scope=actor_private_event in event-kind-registry.json. Reducer-input events (reducer_input=true) carry top-level preconditions / effects / anchor_ref; non-reducer events (read cursor, batch receipts, range completeness, audit RYW, etc.) omit those three fields. Causal refs use prev_refs (actor chain) and refs[] (semantic refs with role: authorized_by, attestation, parent_event, after, recovery_capability, state_witness, inclusion_proof, ...). proof.event_digest is the hash of canonical event bytes minus proofs and unsigned; detached_jws signs the canonical proof binding object that includes event_digest, actor_id, verification_method, created_at, and domain/audience where present. hlc IS included in canonical event bytes (integrity-protected) but is semantically advisory — see encoding.md §6-§7.

**Wire-scope boundary (normative)**: ephemeral_event kinds (ck.presence, ck.typing, ck.receipt.read, ck.call.signal) MUST NOT appear with this schema — they use the dedicated ephemeral-envelope.schema.json carried on the ephemeral channel (and MUST NOT advance Anchor frontier, Move state_root, or reducer state). Likewise ck.key.verification.* kinds use device-message.schema.json on the point-to-point to-device channel. ck.self.events.submit MUST schema_violation any event whose kind has wire_scope=ephemeral_event in the registry — see operations-sync.md §3.6 (wire-scope reject rule).

kind.description: Standard ck.* effect kinds MUST appear in artifacts/registry/event-kind-registry.json. State convergence is defined by event preconditions/effects, Anchor DAG finality, and per-cell Lattice join.

effective_scope.description: Reducer-stamped immutable effective scope for this Event. scope_circle_id=null materializes as {kind:'realm', realm_id}; Circle-scoped objects materialize as {kind:'circle', realm_id, circle_id}. This value enters canonical event bytes and Anchor/sub-anchor leaves; in MLS-backed scopes it also enters E2EE AAD and MLS governance binding input.

executed_by.description: Optional. Present only when an agent acts on behalf of the controller actor. actor_id is the principal of record (controller), executed_by is the agent principal that actually issued the wire write. MUST be a registered native personal agent principal accountable to actor_id (see zh/models/event-and-patch.md and zh/identity/key-management.md agent accountability rules). When present, MUST appear together with authorization_ref. Enters canonical event bytes, event digest, and E2EE AAD. Receivers MUST verify the proof's verification_method maps to executed_by (not actor_id) when this field is present.

authorization_ref.description: Optional. Required when executed_by is present. Prefer a materialized ck:grant:* id; an event id is allowed only when it points to the accepted grant/delegation event that produced the effective authorization. Reducer MUST validate the referenced grant/delegation covers the event kind and target resource and is within its effective validity window.

actor_kind.description: Reducer-stamped projection of the actor_id Actor Profile's actor_kind at write time (see zh/models/event-and-patch.md and zh/models/actor.md). Lets audit/forensic/offline readers classify the event without resolving Actor Profile. MUST NOT appear in actor-supplied submit payload (schema_violation reason=actor_kind_reducer_managed); reducer stamps it during accept. Immutable once written.

hlc.description: Advisory hybrid logical clock. INCLUDED in canonical bytes for signing and event digest (so it is integrity-protected and cannot be rewritten by relays), but semantically advisory: used only as a deterministic tiebreaker for timeline display when two events are causally unreachable. MUST NOT influence authorization, lattice join, Move precondition comparison, or anchor finality. See encoding.md §7 and event-auth-state-resolution.md §3 rule 1.

prev_refs.description: Actor-chain causal predecessors (envelope-level). For semantic refs (authorized_by, after, state_witness, inclusion_proof, ...), use refs[].

refs.description: Semantic refs with role. Roles include: authorized_by, attestation, parent_event, after, audit_pair, recovery_capability, state_witness, inclusion_proof. audit_pair links a privacy-sensitive business event to its ck.audit.accessed record in the same Anchor batch; state_witness/inclusion_proof are critical for conflict-recovery events; see event-auth-state-resolution.md §8.1.

preconditions.description: Reducer-input only. Pre-state predicates that must hold under the anchor_ref view; if any fails, the entire event fails (no partial application of effects).

effects.description: Reducer-input only. Atomic multi-cell CAS writes. MUST contain at least one effect when present.

anchor_ref.description: Reducer-input only. Anchor DAG node this event is submitted against. Receivers MUST verify it is within the Realm's max_anchor_staleness_ms window.

unsigned.description: Local / transport-only metadata (server-derived hints, redaction reason, age). NOT covered by signature or event digest.

proofs.description: Detached signatures over the canonical proof binding object. proof.event_digest is computed from canonical event bytes excluding only proofs and unsigned; hlc is included in that hash as advisory signed metadata. The actor / device / service signature lives here. Anchor signatures live on the Anchor object, not on the event.

requirements.description: Schema/reducer/feature/critical-extension requirements declared by this event. All sub-fields enter the canonical event bytes and the proof event_digest. Receivers MUST fail closed on any unknown critical entry.

schema.description: Schema profile ids this event depends on.

reducer.description: Reducer profile id this event depends on.

features.description: Features this event requires; receiver MUST fail closed if any is unknown.

critical_extensions.description: Critical extension declarations; each entry MUST have id, extension_scope, fail_closed=true.

allOf.$comment: Known active non-reducer event kinds (wire_scope=actor_private_event OR wire_scope=durable_event with reducer_input=false) MUST NOT carry preconditions/effects/anchor_ref. ephemeral_event kinds are forbidden here entirely — see the next allOf branch.

Wire-scope boundary (normative, T02). Kinds with wire_scope=ephemeral_event in event-kind-registry.json MUST NOT appear in the durable Event Envelope. They use ephemeral-envelope.schema.json (broadcast: presence/typing/receipt/call.signal) or device-message.schema.json (point-to-point to-device: ck.key.verification.*). ck.self.events.submit MUST schema_violation on any wire bytes matching this enum; reducer/state path MUST NOT advance Anchor frontier or actor_seq for these kinds.
Known active reducer-input event kinds MUST carry preconditions/effects/anchor_ref. Unknown extension kinds must declare their own critical extension requirements and are not matched by this branch.

Conflict-recovery event detection: any precondition with op=head_in implies conflict recovery semantics. When triggered, refs[] MUST contain BOTH a state_witness and an inclusion_proof (event-auth-state-resolution.md §8.1). Schema-level enforcement; reducer-level verify re-checks.
MUST contain at least one state_witness ref
MUST contain at least one inclusion_proof ref

Reject these top-level field names. The Event Envelope root is closed (additionalProperties=false); extension data belongs in payload or requirements.critical_extensions. The root field names type / auth_refs / target_ref / operation_id are dropped and MUST NOT appear at the root; use kind / refs[role=authorized_by] / payload.* fields / SDK-internal id instead (see operations-sync.md §5).

anyOf.$comment: auth_refs is dropped; it MUST NOT appear at the root, use refs[role=authorized_by]

profile_ref.description: Profile that defines this extension's semantics when schema_ref is not the exact governing profile.

parameters.description: Closed extension-specific parameter bag. Unknown top-level fields are forbidden; extension-defined data belongs here and is interpreted only after id/schema_ref support is confirmed.

material_digest.description: Optional digest of out-of-band extension material when parameters would be too large for the event envelope.

kind.description: add/remove → or_set; set → mv_register/cas_register/lww_register; transition → fsm; inc/dec → counter; append → ordered_log; insert/delete → rga (rga + lww_register require ck.profile.collaborative_text.v1).

element_id.description: RGA element id, format: "<issuer-did>:<seq>". Required for insert/delete ops on rga lattice cells.

predecessor.description: RGA insert: predecessor element id, or the literal "head" for list start.

role.description: Common roles include authorized_by, attestation, parent_event, after, audit_pair, recovery_capability, state_witness, inclusion_proof. audit_pair links a privacy-sensitive business event to its ck.audit.accessed record in the same Anchor batch; state_witness/inclusion_proof are critical for conflict-recovery events; see event-auth-state-resolution.md §8.1.

proof.description: Optional inline proof material. Used for inclusion_proof role: carries the Merkle audit path defined by event-auth-state-resolution.md §4.2 that proves a leaf belongs to a witness state_root. May be omitted when id alone is a content-addressed reference to a separately stored proof object.

kind.description: detached_jws = actor / device / service signature over canonical proof binding object: canonical_json({event_digest, actor_id, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}). event_digest is the canonical event hash excluding only proofs and unsigned; hlc IS covered by that hash as advisory signed metadata. Ordering authority signatures are carried by Anchor.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the Event-signing key. Verifier MUST strip fragment/query only for controller comparison and MUST compare that controller DID bit-identically to actor_id or executed_by according to the accountability rules.

proof.description: Generic detached-JWS proof shape reused by non-Event schemas (snapshot signature, snapshot witness attestations, identity receipts, handle claims, etc.). MUST NOT be used as the shape of Event Envelope `proofs[]` — Event proofs reference $defs/event_proof and bind canonical Event bytes via `event_digest`. drift detection: `payload_digest#event_proof` in forbidden-wire-fields.json is the hard-reject mirror of this rule. New non-Event signed objects MAY $ref this shape; new signed Event-shaped objects MUST instead $ref event_proof.

kind.description: Generic detached JWS proof over a canonical non-Event payload binding object.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the signing key for this non-Event detached proof. Same pattern as $defs/event_proof.verification_method; semantics are decoupled from Event proof (see $defs/event_proof for the Event-only shape).

payload_digest.description: Generic non-Event detached-proof hash. This $defs/proof shape is reused by non-Event schemas; Event.properties.proofs references $defs/event_proof and MUST use event_digest instead.
